intervals.label: detector upgrade (third fill)
intervals.locator: snolab.ca, DEAP-3600 experiment page, status field
intervals.note: SNOLAB's own experiment page (accessed 2026-09-17) states the current status as 'Upgrading'. No source fetched this session gives the true start date of this phase; start is set to 2026-09, the month this status was confirmed, as the earliest date this interval can be anchored to without inventing one -- it is not a claim that the upgrade began that month. Secondary reporting (a 2025 SNOLAB workshop community report, arXiv:2507.11368) associates recent work with a planned 'third fill', but that document's body text could not be retrieved and quoted in this session, so no date from it is recorded. arXiv:2603.27372 (submitted 28 Mar 2026) corroborates ongoing 'hardware upgrades to mitigate residual challenging alpha-backgrounds for WIMP search'. RE-READ 2026-10-25: demoted to a phase annotation. The collaboration's abstracts of 22 June and 21 September 2026 describe a "just-started" / "newly initiated third fill run" with preliminary third-fill results, which conflicts with reading SNOLAB's "Upgrading" status label as a current absence of data taking. The SNOLAB page could not be re-opened. A 2025 plan said third-fill data taking would end "~ summer 2026" with decommissioning to make room for ARGOlite; no fetched source says whether that happened.

Whether third-fill data taking is still running on 2026-10-25 is not stated (the 2025 plan ended it "~ summer 2026"; SNOLAB lists "Upgrading"). RE-CHECK 2026-10-25: the newest dated statement is a 30 July 2026 talk by a DEAP collaboration member: "Now taking data with detector in the upgraded configuration", "New data taking with upgraded detector to mitigate backgrounds (2025 – present)", "New data collection in progress with upgraded DEAP-3600 at SNOLAB". That confirms third-fill running at the end of July 2026 and gives the start year (2025) but not the month; the 21 September 2026 abstract ("newly initiated third fill run", preliminary results) is consistent. No source dated after 21 September reports the end of the run, and the 2025 plan's "~ summer 2026" end is therefore not confirmed. Confidence raised from uncertain to approximate (a talk is a rank-12 source; the start year is approximate).

name: DEAP-3600
notes: DEAP-3600 is a single-phase liquid argon SCINTILLATION detector, not a two-phase time projection chamber: it has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout, and detects only scintillation light via its 255 PMTs, using pulse-shape discrimination of that scintillation signal (deap3600.ca; Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23, Sec. 1). technology_classes lists 'noble_liquid_tpc'/'argon_tpc' only because the ontology's enum has no separate scintillator-only class, per the dark-matter lead's convention in docs/atlas-worklog/dark-matter.md; this should not be read as DEAP-3600 having TPC-style charge readout.

summary.plain: DEAP-3600 is a dark matter experiment 2 km underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It watches 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make hitting an argon nucleus. It has taken data since late 2016 and is currently being upgraded for a further run.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector (no drift field, no ionization/charge readout) at SNOLAB's 2 km level (6000 m.w.e.). Design target of 3600 kg LAr (~3300 kg maintained fill since Nov 2016), 1000 kg fiducial mass within a 55 cm radius, viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs. Sets the leading argon-target WIMP-nucleon exclusion limits above ~30 GeV/c2 and searches for superheavy multi-scattering dark matter; currently in a hardware upgrade phase toward a further ('third') fill.
